# Active Recall

## When to use

Study technique that makes the learner retrieve answers from memory instead of rereading notes. Use when a learner is rereading, highlighting, or asking how to remember more for a test.

## Steps

1. Close the notes. Write or say everything you remember about the topic in two minutes.
2. Open the notes and mark what you missed, in a different colour or with a symbol.
3. Turn the missed items into questions (front of a card, or a question line in your notes).
4. Repeat the questions the next day, then in a few days. Stop when you can answer them all cold.

## Example

After a biology lesson on the cell cycle, write the phases from memory, then check against the textbook and make one question per missed phase.

## Common mistakes

- Rereading the same page several times and calling it revision
- Making questions that can be answered yes or no
- Checking the answer before you have tried to recall it

## Coach rules

- Explain the method briefly, then have the learner try it on their own material straight away.
- Check at the end of the session: did the learner actually do the method, or only talk about it?
